# How deep the backlog is

**Generated by `scripts/build_backlog_depth.py`. Do not edit.**

Every outstanding machine-reading job, placed by the **meeting’s own date** — not by when we discovered it. 6,433 jobs, about $1,396, roughly 2.8 of a week’s allowance.

| stream | one job is | meetings | $ each | $ total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `official` | one meeting’s OFFICIAL minutes, never read: read, structured | 142 | $0.15 | $21 |
| `official-v1` | one meeting’s OFFICIAL minutes, read for votes only: re-read, structured | 4,228 | $0.15 | $621 |
| `reconcile` | one meeting’s two records, compared | 53 | $0.27 | $14 |
| `minutes` | one recording, OUR minutes written from it | 2,010 | $0.37 | $740 |

**The streams are not interchangeable and must not be added into one bar.** `reconcile` can only exist where a recording exists, so its zero before 2025 is the channel’s start date, not neglect.

**3,428 meeting(s) are missing a record outright and are not counted above: 2,377 no town minutes, 1,514 no recording, 220 no transcript.** Not backlog -- there is no command that produces a transcript the town never recorded. Of the missing transcripts, 185 have captions disabled rather than unfetched.

## What this does not say

- When any of this will be done. The sweep runs in whatever allowance is left before the weekly reset, which varies.
- That a zero is an absence. `reconcile` cannot exist before the recordings do, so its zero before 2025 is the channel’s start date and not a gap.
- Whether a missing recording is a technical failure or a board that stopped recording for good. `missing_video` only asks whether the date is on or after the board’s own first dated recording, never whether the board still records today, so a board that recorded once years ago and never again shows every later meeting as missing rather than as a policy change.
